text: development (M 1.2.1) Establish sulfur TES cost target for integration with solar thermal The primary objective was to establish sulfur TES cost target range that meets the criteria of levelized cost of heat (LCOH) from solar thermal + storage < levelized cost of heat for natural gas boiler considering the sensitivity of natural gas price by location and their fluctuations. The technoeconomic model and the sulfur TES capital cost estimation tool were refined throughout the project with feedback from experts identified in Task 1 Page 21 of 87 DE-EE0009329 Element 16 Technologies, Inc. and from manufacturing partners. The technoeconomic model is described in Tasks 4 and 11, and only the key outcomes of Task 2 are summarized below. The best entry markets for solar+TES are regions with high direct normal irradiance (DNI). The U.S. Southwest — California, Nevada, New Mexico, Arizona, Utah, southern part of Wyoming, some parts of Colorado — not only has high DNI [9], but also a significant share of process heat demand [1] in the temperature range of 100-250 oC. For instance, Kurup and Turchi [10] estimated that California alone has approximately 48 TWh of IPH demand below 300 oC. Hence, Element 16 focused the analysis on the US southwest states listed above, with DNI values ranging from 6.1 kWh/m2/day (Sweetwater, WY) to 8.1 kWh/m2/day (Trona, CA). Natural gas prices (𝐶 ) for industrial customers in these states were obtained from 𝑛𝑔 the EIA database [11] and plotted in Fig. 4. The 20-year average natural gas price for all the states plotted in Figure 4 is 6.7 $/MMBTU. Although US states do not have carbon tax currently (some states like CA implement price on carbon via cap-and-trade program), there is a strong consideration from policymakers to implement carbon tax. Hence, we included an 18 $/ton carbon emission price (18 $/ton ~ 1 $/MMBTU) based on the 2020- 2021 average auction settlement price in California’s Cap-and Trade program [12]. This is a conservative assumption as EIA’s 2022 analysis [13], which was reviewed in budget period 1, projected an average carbon emission price of 36 $/ton in the low-carbon scenario for the next 30 years. Developed a dynamic performance model of the line-focusing CST technologies (parabolic trough and linear Fresnel) to conduct annual simulations and verified the model prediction accuracy by comparing it against the results from NREL System Advisor Model (SAM). 2. Developed a simple resistance-network based sulfur TES thermal performance model that was coupled with the solar field performance model to analyze the effects of: a. solar field design parameter - solar multiple; b. sulfur TES design parameter - storage capacity; c. cost parameter - sulfur TES storage cost and natural gas cost; Page 22 of 87 DE-EE0009329 Element 16 Technologies, Inc. d. geographic factors – locations with different direct normal irradiance (DNI) on key performance metrics such as annual plant capacity factor, levelized cost of heat, TES peak charge rate requirement and TES utilization.
